summary: Downward induction on i from n: at i = n positivity is the posSemidef field and lower semicontinuity comes from continuity; from i+1 to i, F is the integral of the corresponding function one level up (the step property), so nonnegativity integrates and Fatou's lemma gives lower semicontinuity.

steps.claim: Prove the statement by decreasing induction on i ≤ n, for all families b and c: the base case is i = n, and the induction step passes from i+1 (hypothesis ih, i+1 ≤ n) to i.
steps.lean: induction' h using Nat.decreasingInduction with i hi ih generalizing b c

steps.claim: Induction step. By ih applied to the families with entry i replaced by u(z), for each z the function one level up is nonnegative (N) and lower semicontinuous (L); by step_sum of K, F at level i is the integral over z of that function (I, e). Rewrite F as this integral, its real part as the integral of real parts, lower semicontinuity as the liminf inequality, and the ofReal of the integral as the lower integral of ofReal (legitimate because the integrand is nonnegative).
steps.lean:
choose N L using fun z ↦ ih _ (update_self _ _ <| b · ·)
  choose I e _ using (K.step_sum hi <| b ·)
  simp_rw [← e, ← integral_re (I _), lowerSemicontinuousAt_iff_le_liminf,
    ofReal_integral_eq_lintegral_ofReal (I _).re (.of_forall (N · _ |>.1))] at *

steps.claim: Hence F ≥ 0 at level i, as an integral of nonnegative functions; and at a continuity point, by Fatou's lemma (∫ liminf ≤ liminf ∫) and the lower semicontinuity L of the integrands, F is lower semicontinuous there.
steps.lean:
use (integral_nonneg <| Function.swap N ·), fun x _ ↦ by
    grw [← lintegral_liminf_le' (I · |>.re.aemeasurable.ennreal_ofReal), L]; fun_prop

steps.claim: Base case i = n: F(x) = 1ᴴ·(J_{n+1}(b(x)_p, b(x)_q))_{p,q}·1 ≥ 0 because the matrix is positive semidefinite (field posSemidef of K, the families share the entry c(x) at n); and F is continuous at x, being a finite sum of the continuous J_{n+1} (field continuous) composed with maps continuous at x, so ofReal ∘ Re ∘ F is continuous, hence lower semicontinuous, at x.
steps.lean:
use by simpa [entrywise] using! (e · |> K.3 _ _ |>.dotProduct_mulVec_nonneg 1),
    fun x _ ↦ ContinuousAt.lowerSemicontinuousAt (ENNReal.continuous_ofReal.continuousAt.comp
      (by cases K; fun_prop))
